required_pattern: Align on the decimal point, drop excess decimals toward zero, keep only the receiver's digits (high-order truncation), drop the sign for an unsigned receiver, never store negative zero.
example_cobol:
01 A PIC S9(5)V99 VALUE -12345.67.
01 B PIC 9(3)V9.
MOVE A TO B.   *> B = 345.6 (sign dropped)
example_target: b.move(a);   // cobolrt CobolDecimal; or: long u = Math.abs(aU / 10) % 10_000;

required_pattern: Copy left to right, pad the receiver with spaces or truncate on the right (JUSTIFIED RIGHT: truncate/pad on the left); reference-modified receivers change only their substring.
example_cobol:
01 X PIC X(5).
MOVE 'ABCDEFG' TO X.   *> 'ABCDE'
example_target: x.move("ABCDEFG");   // cobolrt PicX keeps exactly 5 bytes

required_pattern: Numeric to alphanumeric: the unsigned digit string of the sending PIC (no decimal point), left-justified, space padded. Alphanumeric to numeric: treat the characters as an unsigned integer DISPLAY value of the same length, then store with the receiver's rules.
example_cobol:
01 N PIC S9(3) VALUE -12.
01 X PIC X(5).
MOVE N TO X.   *> '012  '
example_target: x.move(n);   // cobolrt PicX.move(CobolDecimal): unsigned digits, no point, space padded

required_pattern: Copy the raw bytes of the sending item into the receiving group (space padded / truncated), without converting subordinate fields; every elementary field of the receiver is written.
example_cobol:
01 G1. 05 A PIC 9(3). 05 B PIC X(2).
01 G2 PIC X(5).
MOVE G1 TO G2.
example_target: System.arraycopy(g1Bytes, 0, g2Bytes, 0, 5);   // raw record bytes (encode subfields with cobolrt Codec)

required_pattern: Format the value with the receiver's editing symbols (zero suppression, insertion, floating sign) into exactly the edited length.
example_target: // no runtime support yet: implement the PIC editing symbols by hand and test against GnuCOBOL

required_pattern: Concatenate the operands with no separator and end with '\n' (no newline with NO ADVANCING). Numerics print all PIC digits zero-padded, '.' for V, a leading '+'/'-' for signed items (trailing for SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE); X(n) prints exactly n bytes; groups print their raw bytes. Write ISO-8859-1 bytes.
example_cobol:
01 T PIC S9(3)V99 VALUE -1.5.
DISPLAY 'T=' T.   *> T=-001.50
example_target: Display.print(System.out, "T=", t);

required_pattern: Read one line per ACCEPT from stdin (ISO-8859-1). Numeric DISPLAY: window of byte-length characters, de-edit, align, truncate; COMP/COMP-3: whole line; invalid text gives zero; at EOF leave the field unchanged.
example_cobol:
01 A PIC 9(3)V99.
ACCEPT A.   *> input '123.45' stores 123.40
example_target: String line = in.readLine(); if (line != null) a.accept(line);

required_pattern: Evaluate the expression exactly (no intermediate rounding, decimal arithmetic), then store once into each receiver with ROUNDED/truncation and ON SIZE ERROR rules; division by zero is a size error.
example_cobol:
COMPUTE NET ROUNDED = GROSS * RATE / 100
    ON SIZE ERROR MOVE 'Y' TO ERR-FLAG
END-COMPUTE.
example_target: if (net.compute(gross.dec().multiply(rate.dec()).divide(Dec.of(100)), Round.ROUNDED, SizeError.ON)) { errFlag.move("Y"); }

required_pattern: ADD A TO B: B = B + A; ADD A B GIVING C: C = A + B; SUBTRACT A FROM B: B = B - A; MULTIPLY A BY B: B = A * B; DIVIDE A INTO B: B = B / A; DIVIDE A BY B GIVING C [REMAINDER R]. Each receiver is stored with its own truncation/ROUNDED rules; REMAINDER uses the truncated quotient; division by zero leaves receivers unchanged.
example_cobol: DIVIDE 7 INTO A GIVING Q REMAINDER R.
example_target: boolean err = CobolDecimal.divideRemainder(a.dec(), Dec.of(7), q, r, Round.TRUNCATION, SizeError.NONE);   // DIVIDE 7 INTO A: (dividend A, divisor 7)

required_pattern: Round the exact result half away from zero at the store; ADD/SUBTRACT ROUNDED into COMP-3 truncates under GnuCOBOL 3.2.
example_cobol: COMPUTE R ROUNDED = 2.45 * 1.   *> R PIC 9V9 = 2.5
example_target: r.compute(x, Round.ROUNDED, SizeError.NONE);   // x is an exact Dec

required_pattern: If the result does not fit (or a division by zero happens), leave the receiver unchanged and run the SIZE ERROR branch; otherwise store and run NOT ON SIZE ERROR.
example_cobol: ADD 1 TO CNT ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY 'FULL' END-ADD.
example_target: if (cnt.add(1L, Round.TRUNCATION, SizeError.ON)) { Display.print(System.out, "FULL"); }

required_pattern: Numeric comparisons compare values; alphanumeric comparisons pad the shorter operand with spaces and compare bytes; an 88-level name tests its parent against every listed value and THRU range; NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC class tests inspect the bytes.
example_cobol:
05 STATUS-CODE PIC X.
   88 IS-ACTIVE VALUE 'A' 'R'.
IF IS-ACTIVE PERFORM P1 END-IF.
example_target: if (statusCode.equals("A") || statusCode.equals("R")) { p1(); }

required_pattern: Move the first value listed in the 88-level's VALUE clause into its parent, with the parent's MOVE rules.
example_cobol: SET IS-ACTIVE TO TRUE.
example_target: statusCode.move("A");

required_pattern: Test the WHEN clauses in order and run only the first that matches (no fall-through between WHENs); WHEN OTHER is the default; ALSO compares several subjects positionally; THRU ranges are inclusive; EVALUATE TRUE evaluates conditions.
example_cobol:
EVALUATE TRUE
  WHEN AMT > 1000 MOVE 'H' TO BAND
  WHEN AMT > 100  MOVE 'M' TO BAND
  WHEN OTHER      MOVE 'L' TO BAND
END-EVALUATE.
example_target: if (amt.compareTo("1000") > 0) band.move("H"); else if (amt.compareTo("100") > 0) band.move("M"); else band.move("L");

required_pattern: Call the paragraph's parameterless instance method; it returns when execution reaches the end of the paragraph (not at its fall-through).
example_cobol: PERFORM CALC-FEE.
example_target: calcFee();

required_pattern: Run every paragraph from the first to the last in source order, then return; GO TO inside the range that targets the last paragraph's EXIT ends the range.
example_cobol: PERFORM P1 THRU P3.
example_target: p1(); p2(); p3();   // or one method for the whole range when GO TO is involved

required_pattern: Evaluate the count once at entry; run the body that many times (zero or negative: never).
example_cobol: PERFORM P1 N TIMES.
example_target: for (long k = n.unscaled(), i = 0; i < k; i++) p1();   // n is an integer PIC

required_pattern: Test before each iteration (WITH TEST AFTER: after); stop when the condition is true.
example_cobol: PERFORM READ-NEXT UNTIL EOF-FLAG = 'Y'.
example_target: while (!eofFlag.equals("Y")) readNext();

required_pattern: Store FROM into the control field (with its PIC rules), test UNTIL, run the body, add BY (stored with truncation), repeat; AFTER varies the inner item for each outer value; the control field keeps its final value.
example_cobol: PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 3 ADD 1 TO N END-PERFORM.   *> I = 4 afterwards
example_target: for (i.move(1L); i.compareTo("3") <= 0; i.add(1L, Round.TRUNCATION, SizeError.NONE)) n.add(1L, Round.TRUNCATION, SizeError.NONE);

required_pattern: Translate the region reachable by GO TO as one unit using a dispatch loop over paragraph labels; never as a method call that returns.
example_cobol:
P1. IF X = 0 GO TO P3. ...
P2. ...
P3. EXIT.
example_target: int next = P1; loop: while (true) { switch (next) { case P1: if (x == 0) { next = P3; continue loop; } /* falls */ case P2: ...; case P3: break loop; } }
source: Pan et al., ICSE 2024 (control-flow translation bugs)

required_pattern: Flush stdout and end the program with System.exit(RETURN-CODE); GOBACK in the main program is STOP RUN.
example_cobol: MOVE 4 TO RETURN-CODE. STOP RUN.
example_target: System.out.flush(); System.exit(returnCode);

required_pattern: Set every elementary numeric item under the operand to zero and every alphanumeric one to spaces (FILLER and REDEFINES are skipped); VALUE clauses are not re-applied unless WITH ... VALUE is given.
example_cobol: INITIALIZE WS-REC.
example_target: wsRecAmt.move(0L); wsRecName.move("");

required_pattern: Fixed-size array of the OCCURS count; subscript s maps to index s-1; nested OCCURS map to nested arrays.
example_cobol:
05 CELL PIC 9(2) OCCURS 4.
MOVE 7 TO CELL (I).
example_target: cell[(int) i.unscaled() - 1].move(7L);

required_pattern: Keep one byte buffer for the redefined storage; read and write each view through its encoding so a write via one view is visible through the other.
example_cobol:
01 D PIC 9(8).
01 D-PARTS REDEFINES D. 05 YYYY PIC 9(4). 05 MMDD PIC 9(4).
example_target: byte[] d = new byte[8];   // both views decode/encode the same bytes with cobolrt Codec

required_pattern: Open exactly the file named in ASSIGN relative to the working directory (INPUT: read, OUTPUT: truncate, EXTEND: append); set FILE STATUS after each operation; CLOSE flushes.
example_cobol:
SELECT IN-FILE ASSIGN TO 'IN.DAT' ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL FILE STATUS IS FS.
OPEN INPUT IN-FILE.
example_target: in = new BufferedInputStream(new FileInputStream("IN.DAT")); fs.move("00");

required_pattern: LINE SEQUENTIAL: read up to '\n', pad with spaces to the record length, split lines longer than the record; fixed SEQUENTIAL: read exactly the record length. At end: status 10 and the AT END branch; the record area is unchanged.
example_cobol: READ IN-FILE AT END MOVE 'Y' TO EOF-FLAG END-READ.
example_target: byte[] line = readLineBytes(in); if (line == null) { fs.move("10"); eofFlag.move("Y"); } else { inRec.move(line); }   // pad/split per G-FILE

required_pattern: LINE SEQUENTIAL: write the record bytes with trailing spaces trimmed, then '\n'; fixed SEQUENTIAL: write the encoded record bytes with no delimiter.
example_cobol: WRITE OUT-REC.
example_target: out.write(rtrim(outRec.bytes())); out.write('\n');
